title: A refused, locked or replaced pen changes only a status line no screen reader announces
body:
## Summary

## Description

- pair with a wrong PIN under TalkBack
- the PIN box appears; nothing is spoken
- a takeover by another phone is equally silent

## Expected impact
A blind viewer learns why the pen stopped. Could break: chatter if the region also gets heartbeat text.

## Evaluation

Before: 2 of 5 private ranges lanHost ranks are allowed (one only for 10.0.0.0/24)
After: the advertised host is always allowed

instrument: harness case: a fixture that spawns a 15 s sleeper with inherited stdio, RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS=1500; assert the runner returns within 5 s and the sleeper pid is gone; run on Windows and on the Linux CI runner

## Summary
The one owed layering break: desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts loads desk/src/lib/dataDir.ts (a 7-line helper importing only node:path); closing it needs a rule choice the OWED entry already names as the owner's.

## Flow
- owner picks (a), (b) or (c)

title: The Cambridge claim floor can never bind: coverage is 100% at every age
body:
## Summary
claimAllowed() needs VERIFIED and A2 Key coverage >= 90%, but coverage counts a descriptor as practised when any authored scene has one of its skills, so the share is 1.0 for every age 0-99 and the floor is decoration.

## Description
coverage() (desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:109-115) marks a descriptor practised when some allowed scene's skill is in the descriptor's skills list. Each of the eight skills has an authored scene at every age, so all 16 A2 and 23 B1 descriptors read "yes" (tools/cambridge-coverage.cjs prints e.g. "Describe a photograph alone for about a minute [describe] weekend"). The plan's kill criterion (CLAIM_FLOOR = 0.9, desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:119-121) therefore rests on VERIFIED alone; a person flipping VERIFIED turns the Cambridge wording on with no coverage test that could fail. The suite pins coverage numbers derived from the same table (tools/cambridge-rules-test.cjs:54-66), the hand-list-reads-itself shape of §4.7. Fixed would mean a descriptor counts only by a scene that names it (e.g. a `descriptors` field on scenes, or the practice part mapping), so the share can fall below the floor.

## Flow
- for age in 0..99, exam in both: coverage(exam, age).share
- observed: min share 1 (probe)
- consequence: claimAllowed() === VERIFIED for every age

## Expected impact
Before any "A2 Key" claim reaches a screen, the 90% floor would mean something. Could break: tightening the mapping may drop coverage well below 90% and keep the claim off, which is the floor working.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the claim gate has a test that can fail
Before: min coverage share over ages 0-99 and both papers: 1.0 (probe script over coverage())
After: not measurable until a person decides what counts as practising a descriptor; the instrument is the same probe over the new mapping
Method: probe for Before; After needs the teacher's mapping, so the ladder stops at a direction call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
probe: `for age 0..99 for exam of EXAMS: min(coverage(exam,age).share)` -> 1
desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:113 `scenesFor[d.id] = scenes.filter((x) => d.skills.includes(x.skill))`
desk/src/lib/english/cambridge.ts:121 `return VERIFIED && coverage("a2-key-schools", age).share >= CLAIM_FLOOR;`
escalation: direction - what "practised" means for a descriptor is a teacher's call (cambridge.ts asks a teacher to read the table)

title: The goal task puts learner-derived goal text in the instruction, not the data
body:
## Summary
goalTask(aim) interpolates the aim of the learner's goal into the task instruction string; the plan path passes the learner's own words as a data field (learnerAsked) instead.

## Description
The aim comes from k.goal, which the about step's model extracted from what the learner said (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:399), and goalTask writes it inside quotes into `task` (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:71, 180), the field the model reads as instructions; the re-ask does the same (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:201). checkSystem tells the model only the learner's input JSON is untrusted. planAsk, the sibling, keeps the learner's words in `learnerAsked` and refers to it by name (desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:265-266). Registry prompt-safety/untrusted-span-fencing: data carries a provenance label and stays out of the instruction channel. Fixed: put the aim in request.learner.goalAim and say "set this task in learner.goalAim".

## Flow
- learner states a goal in the about questions; the about model returns goal
- advance -> goalTaskDue -> goalTask(aim) -> request.task contains the aim verbatim
- fix: move the aim to a data field, reference it by name, as learnerAsked does

## Expected impact
Learner text stops reaching the instruction channel of the task call; the goal-task behaviour (LG-55) must hold. Could break: the model may set fewer tasks in the goal when the aim is referenced rather than quoted.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - learner-derived text stays in the data channel
Before: learner-derived strings interpolated into an instruction field in check.ts: 2 sites (goalTask, the goal re-ask)
After: predicted 0, with learnerAsked as the pattern; not measured: the behaviour half needs a live run
Method: simulation - walked the LG-55 path and the plan path; the stub gate is S but the goal-task rate needs a live LT run

## Summary

- build the counter instrument; show 2 passes per move
- guard the second pass on fonts.status
- take the stick figure on Walk and Topics moves; keep only if the frame gap does not grow and the fit matches

Less main-thread layout per move on the stick. Could break: a line fitted with fallback metrics if a face loads late and status misreports.

Before: 2 passes per move (code read: lay() then ready.then(lay))
After: predicted 1 pass; stick frame gap unmeasured

title: A limit at infinity whose limit is infinite leaks in its own question, so it is never set
body:
## Summary
leaksCalc and sequenceLeaks treat any mention of infinity as a leak when the truth is infinite, before setting the question's own notation aside, so 'Find lim_(x->infinity) x^2/(x+1).' leaks itself and items.ts drops every such spec - while the sequence-limit set line asks the model for terms that 'grow without bound'.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc.ts:672 leaksCalcOnce: `if (truth.kind === "inf") return /infinit|∞|\binf\b/.test(text);` runs before ownPieces are removed; desk/src/lib/rules/calc2.ts:559 sequenceLeaks the same. desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:422 drops a spec whose printed question leaks. desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:279 (sequence-limit line) and docs/concepts/STUDY-DESK-V2-PLAN.md:666 (ruling 40) ask for terms that 'grow without bound'; docs/MATH-COURSE-PATHS.md:454 rules 'on an infinite limit, the line names infinity at all'. The two rulings conflict: either the infinite case is not a question the desk sets (refuse it in wellFormed, fix the set line), or the leak check sets the question's own 'x -> infinity' aside first (a loosening of a withholding rule). Every hint on such an item a reading page brings in is also withheld (it must say 'as x approaches infinity').

## Flow
- model returns {shape:'sequence-limit', f:'2^x/x^3'} as the set line asks
- wellFormed ok -> question 'Find lim_(n->infinity) a_n, where a_n = 2^n/n^3.' -> leaksCalc(spec, question) true -> dropped
- a page item 'Find lim_(x->infinity) e^x' read by specFromQuestion -> every hint that says 'as x approaches infinity' is refused -> the fixed withheld line

## Expected impact
Owner decides whether divergent limits are asked. Today: 6/9 probed infinite-limit specs are unaskable and their tokens are spent. Could break: under the loosening option, a line that says 'x approaches infinity and so does f' still leaks; a terser 'both go to infinity' would too.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an infinite limit at infinity is either askable or not asked for
Before: 6/6 well-formed infinite limits at +-infinity (3 sequences, 3 limits) leak in their own printed question; 0/3 finite ones do
After: unmeasurable until the direction is chosen: option A (refuse in wellFormed) gives 0 asked and 0 wasted; option B (pieces first) gives 0/6 self-leaks
Method: probe - question() and leaksCalc on 9 specs; the rung above needs the ruling
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen

title: English arccot, arcsec, arccsc are unreadable while Czech arccotg reads
body:
## Summary
The expression engine has no arccot/acot/arcsec/arccsc, so an English learner's 'arccot(x) + C' is 'cannot read', while a Czech learner's 'arccotg(x) + C' is judged right through czechNames.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/calc-expr.ts:103-113 WORDS has arcsin/arccos/arctan only; desk/src/lib/rules/calc-read.ts czechNames maps arccotg to (pi/2 - arctan(u)). Stewart (the course text) uses cot^-1 and arccot. Fix shape: add arccot/acot as a reading (FnName, FNS, TEX_FN, chain.ts OUTER - Record<FnName> forces all four), or expand 'arccot u' the way czechNames does for every learner. M across calc-expr and chain.

## Flow
- uk learner answers int -1/(1+x^2) dx with 'arccot(x) + C' -> compile null -> unsure 'cannot read'
- cz learner writes 'arccotg(x) + C' -> right
- specFromQuestion('Differentiate f(x) = arccot(x)') -> null; the cz form reads

## Expected impact
English Calculus learners can use the inverse cotangent the textbook teaches. Could break: the lexer's longest-first split ('arccos' vs 'arccot') and the frozen table.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the inverse cot reads in English as it does in Czech
Before: compile('arccot(x)') null; 4/4 English forms unreadable; checkAnswer English 'unsure', Czech 'right'
After: expected 4/4 readable, verdicts equal across systems (not built)
Method: simulation - three walked answers and one page text; the build crosses two files and the lexer

title: The tick loop re-arms after onStop and can crash the process after onDestroy
body:
## Summary
onStop removes the tick, but a probe already in flight re-posts it; after onDestroy the next tick submits to a shut-down executor.

## Description
`StickActivity.kt:151` removes the tick on stop, but every probe callback ends in `schedule()` (`StickActivity.kt:275`, `:286`, via `apply`), and `probe()` posts its answer whatever the lifecycle (`StickActivity.kt:203`, gated only by `gen`). So a Home press while a probe is in flight (often on the error screen: a failing connect takes 2 s of each 5 s tick) leaves the loop probing in the background for good, and a recovery there loads /tv in a stopped activity. After Back-leave, `onDestroy` (`StickActivity.kt:152`) shuts the executor down without bumping `gen`; the in-flight answer re-arms the tick, and the next `io.execute` throws RejectedExecutionException on the main thread. Registry: native-shell-integration (creation-names-reaper: the loop and the executor have no reaper). Fix: a started flag that schedule() honours, gen++ and removeCallbacks in onStop/onDestroy, and busy cleared when an answer is dropped.

## Flow
- error screen, a probe in flight -> Home
- probe answers -> schedule() re-arms -> probes every 5 s while stopped
- or: Back-leave with a probe in flight -> onDestroy shuts io -> answer re-arms -> tick -> io.execute -> RejectedExecutionException

## Expected impact
The stick stops probing the desk from the background and leaves without a crash. Could break: the resume path (onStart must restart the loop after a dropped answer cleared busy).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the loop stops when the activity stops
Before: simulated: a probe in flight at onStop re-arms the tick (3 schedule() call sites reachable from a probe answer); after onDestroy the next tick hits a shut-down executor
After: predicted: no probe log lines after Home; no FATAL after leaving from the error screen
Method: simulation - three walked cases (Home on the error screen, Home on the page, Back-leave during a probe); no device in this session and no Robolectric in the module
Result: better
Gate: none

_Lane B: A/B-drainable with /scan-sweep --ab-only (instrument: device: desk stopped, stick on the error screen; press Home within 2 s of a 'probe' log line; `adb logcat -s StickKeys` must show no 'probe' line after Home for 30 s; then Back-leave during a probe and grep logcat for 'FATAL EXCEPTION' / RejectedExecutionException)._

title: The heartbeat reads the whole TV session; one over 4 MB reads as not a desk
body:
## Summary
The probe reads up to 4 MB of the TV's full session to find `viewer`, which the TV view puts last; past the cap the probe fails and three in a row drop the page.

## Description
`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/DeskNet.kt:56-62` buffers the body up to 4 MB, every heartbeat (BEAT_MS 10 s) and every scan probe. For the TV, `view()` returns `{ ...seen, viewer: "tv" }` (`desk/src/lib/session/pairing.ts:277`) and `viewer` is not a stored key (`desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:393-394`), so it is the LAST key: the probe needs the whole body, and when the session (history, memory, pages, essays) passes 4 MB `Probe.read` (`stick-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/studydesk/stick/Desk.kt:131-132`) returns 'something answered, but not a Study Desk'. That collapses 'unverifiable' into 'failed' (registry: health-checks/three-state-outcomes), and three of those take the page down. Fix: stream the body keeping its head and a rolling tail (64 KB each), and read the fields from those; the heap per beat falls with it.

## Flow
- a TV session grows past 4 MB
- heartbeat: the 4 MB head has no viewer -> Failed
- three beats -> the error screen over a running desk
- fix: head+tail read -> Answered(tv), at 128 KB per probe

## Expected impact
A large session no longer looks like a dead desk, and each heartbeat holds kilobytes, not megabytes, on a 1 GB stick. Could break: a body whose fields sit in the middle (not the desk's shape).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a large session is still recognised; performance - bounded heap per heartbeat
Before: body held per probe: up to 4 MB; a >4 MB TV session -> Failed
After: predicted: 128 KB; Answered(tv)
Method: simulation - the JVM reproduction (an HttpServer serving 5 MB with viewer last) and the real TV-view size are the instrument; this round built the contract test instead
Result: better
Gate: none

_Lane B: A/B-drainable with /scan-sweep --ab-only (instrument: JVM test with com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer serving a 5 MB JSON with viewer last (Failed before, Answered after) plus `JSON.stringify(view(s,'tv')).length` over the seeded test sessions to size the real body)._

title: The phone's thumbnail is the nearest keyframe, not the paused frame
body:
## Summary
Thumbnailer pulls frames with OPTION_CLOSEST_SYNC, so the picture the phone draws over can be up to half a GOP away from the frame the TV shows.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Thumbnailer.kt:14 promises 'the frame the viewer is looking at'; :80 asks MediaMetadataRetriever for the closest SYNC frame. The fixture is encoded with -g 25 at 25 fps (fixtures/README.md:10), one keyframe a second, so a pause between keyframes yields a thumbnail up to 0.5 s off; the fixture's orange box moves ~140 px/s, so up to ~70 px of 1280 (5.5 % of the width) away from where the TV shows it. Real footage has longer GOPs (2-10 s). OPTION_CLOSEST returns the exact frame at the cost of decoding from the previous keyframe. Technique: media-playback / transport-contract (the phone's picture must match the engine's state).

## Flow
- pause the TV at t = 10.48 s -> heartbeat asks dataUrlAt(10480) -> CLOSEST_SYNC returns the 10.0 s keyframe -> the phone shows the box ~67 px left of the TV's box -> the viewer draws on the wrong spot

## Expected impact
Viewers drawing from the phone hit what they see on the TV. Could break: a slower decode delays the state heartbeat once per pause on the Stick.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the phone's picture is the TV's paused frame
Before: simulation - fixture GOP 25 at 25 fps: worst-case offset 0.5 s = ~70 px at 140 px/s; three pauses (10.04, 10.48, 10.96 s) -> keyframes 10.0, 10.0, 11.0 s -> offsets 6, 67, 6 px

title: Two spotlights at once: the second dims the first's highlight
body:
## Summary

title: The 30 Hz playhead tick recomposes the whole TV screen, not just the overlay
body:
## Summary
TelestratorScreen keeps the playhead in Compose state it reads in its own body, so every 33 ms tick recomposes the screen composable and everything it calls, including the pairing card.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:195 `var tMs by remember { mutableLongStateOf(0L) }` is written every 33 ms (:213) and read in TelestratorScreen's body (passed to TelestrationOverlay and the status Text), as are paused and rate. Session is an unstable parameter, so PairingCard is not skipped either. Technique: media-playback / playback-clock (a frame clock is not reactive state; consumers sample at their own cadence). Fix: hand the overlay a State<Long>/lambda and read it inside the Canvas draw (draw-phase read), and move the status line's reads into its own small composable.

## Flow
- play the clip -> tick writes tMs -> TelestratorScreen recomposes ~30x/s -> PairingCard, AndroidView update, overlay recompose
- fix: draw-phase read of the playhead; the screen recomposes only on doc, link or peek changes

## Expected impact
Less main-thread work per frame on the Stick, where the overlay budget is 4 ms and GC churn is a measured cost. Could break: the overlay must still redraw when tMs changes (a draw-phase read invalidates draw).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - screen recompositions per second of playback
Before: simulation - ~30 recompositions/s of TelestratorScreen during playback (one per tick) from the read sites
After: predicted ~0/s of the screen body; overlay draws stay ~30/s

title: Voice probe's firstAudioMs loses its index when a line starts and then errors
body:
## Summary
VoiceProbeActivity appends to firstAudioMs on onStart and again (-1) on onError, so a line that starts and then fails writes two entries and every later index is shifted, against the report's own documented shape.

## Description
tv-app/src/debug/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/voiceprobe/VoiceProbeActivity.kt:30 documents 'firstAudioMs[i] is -1 for a line that never started'; :104 onStart appends the latency and :107 onError appends -1. An utterance can call onStart then onError (an engine that fails mid-line), giving 13 entries for 12 lines, and the operator's device run (docs/concepts/NATIVE-VOICE-STACK.md) reads the wrong latency for every later line. Fix: put by index (pass * lines.size + i) and write -1 only if that index never started.

## Flow
- line 3 starts (put 210) then errors (put -1) -> array [.., 210, -1, <line 4>, ..] -> line 4 reads -1
- fix: firstAudioMs.put(index, value); onError writes -1 only when no start was recorded

## Expected impact
The operator's TTS latency figures per line stay true on an engine that errors. Could break: nothing outside the debug probe.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the report matches its documented shape
Before: simulation - three runs: all lines OK -> 12 entries aligned; one never-started line -> 12 aligned; one start-then-error line -> 13 entries, 9 misaligned (if it is line 3)
After: predicted: 12 entries aligned in all three
Method: simulation - org.json is a stub on the JVM, so a test needs the recorder extracted into plain Kotlin first
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The pen listener admits any peer address class before the PIN gate
body:
## Summary
LanTransport binds 0.0.0.0 and serves /, /health and /ws to any peer, with no address-class check in front of the pairing gate, which the governing technique names as layer one.

## Description
Technique: device-pairing / admission-scoping ('classify the peer before you compute'; 'bind-address and peer-class must agree; test the refusal'). tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt:111 binds host 0.0.0.0, and penServer (:159-160) answers /health (session telemetry: annotations, pens, playhead) and opens /ws for every peer. The intended audience is the LAN: private, link-local and loopback (adb forward arrives as 127.0.0.1; the emulator host as 10.0.2.2). A TV with a public or carrier-NAT address, or a port-forward, exposes the pairing door and the PIN guess budget to the internet. Fix: an isAdmissiblePeer(remoteHost) classifier (incl. IPv4-mapped IPv6) refusing others with a cheap 403 before any pairing work, with a unit test.

## Flow
- peer from a public address connects to :8765/ws -> admitted -> may spend the shared wrong-PIN budget (locking out the household)
- fix: classify call.request.local.remoteHost; refuse non-private peers on all three routes

## Expected impact
The pairing door is only reachable from the room's network. Could break: a home network on CGNAT ranges (100.64/10) or an unusual emulator route if the classifier is too strict.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - only LAN peers reach the pairing gate
Before: peer classes refused before the PIN gate: 0
After: all non-loopback/private/link-local peers refused
Method: simulation - the classifier test is S, but whether real living-room networks all fall in the admitted classes needs the harness walk on the emulator and the Stick
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

_Lane B: A/B-drainable with /scan-sweep --ab-only (instrument: isAdmissiblePeer unit test (public, private, link-local, loopback, ::ffff:-mapped) plus live-ui-test.mjs and relay-test.mjs on the emulator to prove adb-forwarded and LAN peers still pair)._
